description: An age-of-sail archipelago. Wet islands, tar and cordage, and a port every few hours' sail; an errand here is a cargo and everybody is owed something.

appearance.chandler: Everything a ship needs behind him, and he knows where all of it is.
appearance.cooper: Hands pale with shavings, a half-hooped barrel between the knees.
appearance.sailmaker: A palm strapped to one hand, pushing a needle through weather.
appearance.ropewalker: Backing away down the length of the shed while he talks to you.
appearance.boatswain: Ashore, unhappy about it, and dressed for a wind that is not blowing.
appearance.pilot: Watching the water past your shoulder the whole time.
appearance.harbour master: A book, a pen, and a list you are not yet on.
appearance.clerk: Ink to the knuckle and half an ear on the door.
appearance.netmender: Mending, with the work hooked over one bare toe.
appearance.tallyman: A slate, a stub of chalk, and a very poor opinion of your timing.

talksAbout.harbour master: what is in the roads, what is owed on it, and what is not coming back
talksAbout.pilot: the bar, the tide over it, and the three men who got it wrong
talksAbout.chandler: prices, and the tar, which has not come up from the south this year
talksAbout.boatswain: the crew he had, and the crew he has been given
talksAbout.sailmaker: canvas, and the difference between the two sorts nobody else can see
talksAbout.factor: the manifest, the shortfall, and whose signature is on both
talksAbout.cooper: the staves, and who is buying barrels for what

lore.title: The Standing Charter
lore.premise: A charter that gave three families the whole trade of these islands has lapsed, and nobody can find the copy that says when. Two ships are sitting in the roads waiting to hear whose cargo they are carrying.
lore.era: the last year of the old charter

ambient: The wind has been in the same quarter for three days and everyone has stopped mentioning it.
Tar, rope and low tide, in that order.
Something is knocking against a hull out in the dark, patiently.
The gulls have gone quiet, which is worse than the noise.
Every roof here faces the same way, and it is not the way the road runs.

warehouse: Three-strand, tarred, and heavy as a person.
Number four canvas, and stiff with new.
Stoppered, and sweating in the warm.
Packed in layers, and it announces itself.
shop: Horn panes, and one of them mended with wax.
Forty feet of it, waxed against the wet.
hall: Wax, ribbon, and a date somebody has been at with a knife.
Every keel in and out, in three hands, none of them tidy.
inn: Cut with something. Everything here is.
house: Bone, and worn to a shine at the grip.
smithy: A twist of them, clenched square.
Offcuts and failures, kept for remelting.
ruin: The ink has run, but the amounts have not.
Old currency, of a mint nobody here uses.

shop: Three-strand, tarred, sold by the fathom.
For the seams, the standing rigging, and the boots.
Horn panes, and one of them mended with wax.
Stiff, foul-smelling, and the only dry thing you will own.
For the hull, and for anything you would rather was not seen.
cooper: Sound, sworn to, and it will be your problem if it is not.
Weak enough to drink all day, which is the point.
sailmaker: Number four canvas. Sold by the ell and cut in front of you.
Leather, brass, and shaped to one hand only.
For the edge of anything that has to hold.
warehouse: Packed in layers, and it announces itself.
Bleeds red into water. The dyers pay well for it.
Signed and sealed, and worth exactly what it says.
inn: Older than the voyage it was baked for.
Straw mattress, shared room, no questions.
smithy: A twist of them, clenched square.
Four flukes, and a ring worn oval.
apothecary: Smells terrible. Closes a cut in a day.
Cloudy, and warm to the touch.
Sharp enough to make your ears ring. Keeps the teeth in.

marsh: Salt already, which saves carrying any.
Sodden, and it holds far more water than it looks able to.
reeds: A bundle of them, still wet at the ends.
Whippy, and they will bend into anything.
bush: Coconut, unaccountably, and they sting to gather.
Sour past the point of comedy. They keep.
sand: Raked up in a minute, and worth the wet knees.
rock: Prised off with a stone, and about as good as that sounds.
It takes a hard edge and a harder spark.
gravel: Piled in the tideline, sorted by the sea.
forestFloor: Pale, and growing in a rough ring.
Dry twigs, gathered by the handful.
